STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.claim: The surah opens by describing the virtues and righteous actions of believers.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.anchor: begins by describing the virtues and righteous actions of those who believe

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p241/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p241/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p241/r4.claim: Trusts include God-given capacities, duties, blessings, entrusted property, and social responsibilities; covenants include those grounded in human nature or revelation and every explicit or customary promise to God or people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p241/r4.anchor: ﻣٰﻨٰﺖ  refers to all trusts which our Lord has blessed us with in the form of strengths, abilities, obligations and responsibilities

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p241/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p241/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p241/r5.claim: The believers described are faithful to God and other people, neither rebelling against the Lord nor betraying creatures or breaking their word.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p241/r5.anchor: They are neither dishonest and rebellious in the matter of their Lord nor are ones who are unfaithful to His creatures

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p242/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p242/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p242/r1.claim: The trust-and-promise verse comprehensively gathers religious, moral, legal, and social duties revered by every sharīʿah; its details are distributed throughout the Qur'an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p242/r1.anchor: Here it is a comprehensive statement made after the earlier directives and is in fact a detail of what is concise

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p242/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p242/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p242/r2.claim: Prayer protects all covenants because it is itself a covenant with the Lord, renewed five times daily, and recalls the believer's other promises and responsibilities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p242/r2.anchor: The prayer itself, as is evident from the explanation of S ūrah al-Baqarah, is a person’s covenant with his Lord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.claim: Al-Mu'minūn's opening describes success through humble prayer, avoiding frivolity, zakāh, chastity and restraint, trustworthiness, and keeping promises.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.anchor: salvation and success before God is reserved for those believers whose prayers are marked with humility and concentration

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read أمانة in the singular; the remaining seven readers use the plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو في رواية لأمانتهم بالإفراد وباقي السبعة بالجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r3.claim: Amanah may broadly include everything God entrusted to a servant—speech, action, belief, duties, and prohibitions—or specifically the trusts people place with one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r3.anchor: والظاهر عموم الأمانات فيدخل فيها ما ائتمن تعالى عليه العبد من قول وفعل واعتقاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r4.claim: Amanah is the entrusted thing; safeguarding it means preserving it until delivery. The word can also denote the act of entrusting, but the delivered item or statement is the object, not the verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r4.anchor: هي الشيء المؤتمن عليه ومراعاتها القيام عليها لحفظها

SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir reads singular here and in al-Maʿārij; the others read plural, which al-Samīn says better fits the intended generality.

SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r2.claim: Amāna is originally a verbal noun, but it can also denote the entrusted thing itself, as in the cited verses.
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r2.anchor: الأمانة في الأصل مصدر، ويطلق على الشيء

SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that the commands to return and not betray trusts concern entrusted objects, since objects rather than abstract meanings are returned or betrayed.
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r3.anchor: إنما يؤدى ويخان الأعيان لا المعاني، كذا قال الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r4.claim: Al-Samīn accepts al-Zamakhsharī's point about those two verses but says this verse can mean either the abstract trust or the entrusted object.
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r4.anchor: أما ما ذكره من الآيتين فمسلم

ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r6.claim: The word أماناتهم is read in both singular and plural forms.
ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r6.anchor: والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون (8) ويقرأ لأمانتهم واحدا وجمعا.

ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r7.claim: Rāʿūn means tending and protecting trusts and covenants; the root denotes taking responsibility to put what one oversees in good order.
ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r7.anchor: وأصل الرعي في اللغة القيام على إصلاح ما يتولاه الراعي من كل شيء تقول: الإمام يرعى رعيته،

ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r3.claim: The successful keep trusts and pledges and guard their prayers from worldly intent.
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r3.anchor: and who guard their prayers [from all worldly intent].

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r5.claim: He notes that both sūrahs repeat the rules on guarding chastity, its stated exceptions, and faithfully keeping trusts and covenants.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r5.anchor: قال في سورتي (المؤمنون) و (المعارج) : {والذين هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p287/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p287/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p287/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir alone reads amānatihim in the singular.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p287/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p287/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p287/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the plural form amānātihim.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p255/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p255/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p255/r5.claim: The singular reading is supported by the following singular عهدهم, rather than a plural form.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p255/r5.anchor: فمن وحد استدل بقوله وعهدهم ولم يقل وعهودهم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p255/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p255/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p255/r6.claim: The plural reading is supported by the command to return trusts to their owners.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p255/r6.anchor: ومن جمع استدل بقوله ﴿ أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p444/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p444/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p444/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr alone reads the trusts in singular; the other readers use plural.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p444/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وحده / لأمنتهم / واحدة وقرأ الباقون / لأمنتهم / جماعة

QIRAAT-ER:23:8:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:8:5#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:23:8:5#1/r1.claim: The singular amāna treats trust as one abstract concept, while plural amānāt individualizes the obligations.
QIRAAT-ER:23:8:5#1/r1.anchor: Lvw, mutawatir: Singular amānatihim vs standard plural amānātihim — singular treats trust as a unified abstract concept

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r1.claim: Rāʿūn means actively preserving; the root first described protecting livestock through feeding it or warding off enemies, then generalized to preservation.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r1.anchor: قائمون يحفظها واصطلاحها وأصل الرعي حفظ الحيوان إما بغذائه الحافظ لحياته

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r2.claim: Amānāt is the plural of amāna, originally a verbal noun, but here means entrusted things to preserve, especially property rather than an abstract act; its plural form does not settle the issue because verbal nouns can be plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r2.anchor: وأما جمعها فلا يعين ذلك إذ المصادر قد تجمع كما قدمنا غير بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r3.claim: ʿAhd is likewise a verbal noun used here for the concrete covenant or undertaking to be kept.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r3.anchor: وكذا العهد مصدر أريد به ما عوهد عليه لذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r4.claim: Most commentators read the verse broadly: believers keep everything entrusted or covenanted with them by God and people, including religious duties, deposits, oaths, vows, and agreements.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r4.anchor: والآية عند أكثر المفسرين عامة في كل ما ائتمنوا وعوهدوا من جهة الله تعالى ومن جهة الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r5.claim: Amānāt is plural because each person faces many diverse trusts from God, while covenants are not comparably numerous for every person.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r5.anchor: وجمعت الأمانة دون العهد لأنها متنوعة متعددة جدا بالنسبة إلى كل مكلف من جهته تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r6.claim: Some commentators limit the trusts and covenants to those placed upon believers by other people; Al-Ālūsī says this is not persuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r6.anchor: وجوز بعض المفسرين كونها خاصة فيما ائتمنوا عليه وعوهدوا من جهة الناس وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī also understands trusts as bodily members and faculties entrusted by God; preserving them means not using them contrary to His command.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r7.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن يراد بالأمانات ماائتمنهم الله تعالى عليه من الأعضاء والقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r8.claim: The covenant may be God's command in His Book and through His Messenger; keeping it means fulfilling it fully. Trust-keeping is like removing defilement, while covenant-keeping is adornment.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r8.anchor: وأن يراد بالعهد ما عاهدهم الله تعالى عليه مما أمرهم به سبحانه بكتابه وعلى لسان رسوله

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r9.claim: Alternatively, amānāt can include money and similar trusts generally, with the plural reflecting their plainly observable numerical multiplicity.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن تعمم الأمانات بحيث تشمل الأموال ونحوها وجمعها لما فيها لمن التعدد المحسوس المشاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r10.speaker: ابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r10.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr have a reading with the singular لأمانتهم.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p11/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو في رواية ( لأمانتهم ) بالإفراد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir reads amanat in the singular here and in al-Maʿarij, associating it with the singular covenant; the other readers use the plural, as in the cited command to return trusts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r11.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير "لأمانتهم" على التوحيد هاهنا وفي سورة المعارج، لقوله تعالى: "وعهدهم" والباقون بالجمع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r12.claim: They safeguard what has been entrusted to them and fulfill covenants they made with other people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r12.anchor: {وعهدهم راعون} حافظون، أي: يحفظون ما ائتمنوا عليه، والعقود التي عاقدوا الناس عليها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r13.claim: Trusts include duties between God and a servant, such as prayer, fasting, and other required worship, as well as interpersonal trusts such as deposits and services; all must be fulfilled.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r13.anchor: والأمانات تختلف فتكون بين الله تعالى وبين العبد كالصلاة والصيام والعبادات التي أوجبها الله عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:7-10/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:7-10/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:7-10/r3.claim: Their trusts and covenants include what is entrusted or promised on behalf of God or people; they preserve and set them right.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:7-10/r3.anchor: لما يؤتمنون عليه ويعاهدون من جهة الحق أو الخلق.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:7-10/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:7-10/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:7-10/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads singular amānah here and in al-Maʿārij, either to avoid ambiguity or because the singular is the original verbal noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:7-10/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير هنا وفي «المعارج» { لأمانتهم } على الإفراد ولأمن الإلباس

DURR-FULL:v6p87/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p87/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p87/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says trusts are what people entrust to one another, covenants are fulfilled, and guardianship means preserving them.
DURR-FULL:v6p87/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون} يعني: الأموال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r1.claim: This quality comprises two major virtues: faithfully returning trusts and keeping covenants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r1.anchor: هذه صفة أخرى من جلائل صفات المؤمنين تنحل إلى فضيلتين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r2.claim: A trust is often a valuable object privately left with someone thought reliable; its value and lack of witnesses tempt the trustee to retain or deny it, so returning it is a branch of faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r2.anchor: فهي لنفاستها قد تغري الأمين عليها بأن لا يردها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r3.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r3.claim: Hudhayfa reports the Prophet saying trust settled deep in people's hearts, was learned from Qur'an and Sunna, then was withdrawn during sleep until people rarely returned trusts; apparent competence no longer signaled faith. No grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r3.anchor: عن حذيفة بن اليمان قال ( حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r4.claim: Wakt is a dark mark on date skin; majal is a raised swelling on thin skin, likened to grape skin, from fire or repeated handwork.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r4.anchor: الوكت : سواد يكون في قشر التمر . والمجل : انتفاخ في الجلد الرقيق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r5.claim: The hadith's mustard-seed measure means the trust people place in someone, not faith inside him; only a gullible person would entrust him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r5.anchor: هو مصدر آمنه ، أي وما في قرارة نفسه شيء من إيمان الناس إياه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur previously discussed trusts under the verse commanding that they be delivered to their owners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r6.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام على الأمانة في قوله تعالى : { إن الله يأمركم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r7.claim: The plural reflects the many kinds of trusts and people entrusted with keeping them, explicitly emphasizing generality.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r8.claim: The majority read the word in the plural.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r9.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the singular amanah as a verbal noun, comparable to the wording for humility in prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p15#2/r9.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير { لأمانتهم } بالإفراد باعتبار المصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r1.claim: A covenant is a commitment between two or more parties about how they will treat one another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r1.anchor: والعهد : التزام بين اثنين أو أكثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r2.claim: The name covenant reflects both parties pledging by God, who oversees the agreement and can hold them accountable for breach.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r2.anchor: وسمي عهدا لأنهما يتحالفان بعهد الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur previously discussed the covenant under the verse about those who break God's covenant after its binding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r3.anchor: وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { الذين ينقضون عهد الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r4.claim: Keeping covenants is a great virtue showing nobility and resolve; people may betray burdensome duties for another's benefit out of greed or weak resolve.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r4.anchor: والوفاء بالعهد من أعظم الخلق الكريم لدلالته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r5.claim: The Qur'an says a covenant will be called to account, reinforcing the moral weight of keeping it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r5.anchor: قال تعالى : { وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسؤولا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r6.claim: Watching over means preserving something from loss and repairing what decays; it also describes tending livestock or people and, metaphorically, treating people well.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r6.anchor: والرعي : مراقبة شيء بحفظه من التلاشي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r7.claim: Watching over a trust means preserving it, with return to its owner as the purpose; watching over a covenant is keeping it in view whenever relevant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r7.anchor: فرعي الأمانة : حفظها ، ولما كان الحفظ مقصودا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r8.claim: The fronted phrase and repeated relative pronoun follow the pattern of the preceding qualities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r8.anchor: والقول في تقديم { لأماناتهم وعهدهم } على { راعون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r9.claim: Trusts and covenants are joined because a person who makes a covenant entrusts the other party to fulfill it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r9.anchor: والجمع بين رعي الأمانات ورعي العهد لأن العهد كالأمانة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r10.claim: This trait follows zakah because wealth given is God's trust, called the right of God, the right of wealth, and the right of the poor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p17/r10.anchor: وذكرهما عقب أداء الزكاة لأن الزكاة أمانة الله عند الذين أنعم عليهم بالمال

BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r1.claim: The trusts and covenants include what people entrust to them or bind themselves to, whether from God or from other people; examples include deposits and duties such as prayer, fasting, and ritual bathing.
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r1.anchor: لما يؤتمنون عليه ويعاهدون من جهة الحق أو الخلق

BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r2.claim: An amana is what a person is entrusted with; an ahd is maintaining and attending to something over time, including a binding compact.
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r2.anchor: والأمانة اسم لما يؤتمن عليه الإنسان والعهد حفظ الشيء ومراعاته حالا بعد حال

BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r3.claim: Guarding means maintaining and protecting these trusts and covenants in a sound way.
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r3.anchor: أي قائمون عليها وحافظون لها على وجه الإصلاح

BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r4.claim: Najmiyya identifies the human trust as the divine outpouring received without intermediary, a special honor of humankind; the covenant is the primordial pledge to worship God alone, as in 36:61.
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r4.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : الأمانة التي حملها الإنسان وهي الفيض الإلهي بلا واسطة

BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r5.claim: Keeping the inner and outer trusts entails worshipping no other than God; desire is the most hateful idol because it makes people worship what they worship besides God.
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r5.anchor: راعون بأن لا يخونوا في الأمانات الظاهرة والباطنة ولا يعبدوا غير الله

BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r6.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl says all limbs are trusts: eyes must avoid forbidden sights and reflect, ears avoid idle or obscene speech and attend remembrance, and the tongue avoid backbiting and slander while remembering God.
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r6.anchor: قال محمد بن الفضل : جوارحك كلها أمانات عندك أمرت في كل واحدة منها

BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r7.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl assigns the feet to obedience, the mouth to lawful intake, and the hands to avoiding what is unlawful and not withholding what is good.
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r7.anchor: وأمانة الرجل المشي إلى الطاعات والتباعد عن المعاصي

BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r8.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl says the heart's trust is constant regard for God, seeing and witnessing no other and finding repose only in Him.
BURSEVI:v6p48#4/r8.anchor: وأمانة القلب مراعاة الحق على دوام الأوقات حتى لا يطالع سواه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r1.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r1.claim: The majority read “amānāt” in the plural.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir reads “amānat” in the singular.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r3.claim: Trust encompasses every religious and worldly duty a person bears in word or deed, including social dealings and promises.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r3.anchor: والأمانة العهد تجمع كل ما تحمله الإنسان من أمر دينه ودنياه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r4.claim: Trust is broader than covenant: every covenant is a trust, while some trusts require no prior covenant; as God's charge to people, both stand equally.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r4.anchor: والأمانة أعم من العهد، إذ كل عهد فهو أمانة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p137#2/r5.claim: Guarding these trusts means preserving them and fulfilling them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the phrase in the singular, amānatihim, as a generic noun for the trusts placed in their care.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r1.anchor: والذين هم لأماناتهم قرأ أبن كثير لأمانتهم وهو اسم جنس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r2.claim: Trusts may be duties owed to God or to other people; they must observe all of them, as well as their covenants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r2.anchor: فتارة تكون الأمانة بين العبد وبين ربه وتارة تكون بينه وبين جنسه فعليه مراعاة الكل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r3.claim: Rāʿūn means guardians or keepers; the root describes a shepherd tending to improve what is entrusted to him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p461#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى راعون حافظون قال الزجاج وأصل الرعي في اللغة القيام على اصلاح ما يتولاه الراعي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the immediately preceding report gharīb and says its chain contains an unidentified narrator; this segment supplies no further report content.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r1.anchor: هذا حديث غريب، وإسناده فيه من لا يعرف؛ لجهالته، والله أعلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r2.claim: Believers do not betray entrusted things but return them to their owners, and they fulfill covenants and agreements.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r2.anchor: أي: إذا اؤتمنوا لم يخونوا، بل يؤدونها إلى أهلها، وإذا عاهدوا أو عاقدوا أوفوا بذلك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r3.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r3.claim: The Prophet describes the hypocrite by three traits: lying when speaking, breaking promises, and betraying a trust.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p463/r3.anchor: لا كصفات المنافقين الذين قال فيهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "آية المنافق ثلاث: إذا حدث كذب،

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads أمانتهم in the singular, as in Sūrat al-Maʿārij, in agreement with عهدهم.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير: (والذين هم لأمانتهم) على واحد وفي (المعارج) مثله

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r5.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r5.claim: The other readers use the plural أماناتهم, matching the plural wording in 4:58.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r5.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: (لأماناتهم) على الجمع اعتبارا بقوله

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.claim: The listed traits remove ambiguity: whoever has them is a believer, supporting the author’s position.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.anchor: ثم بين تعالى ما أزال كل شبهة، فذكر صفات المؤمن، فدل أن من كانت صفته ما ذكر

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r15.claim: The verse requires keeping trusts and covenants, including all trusts and liabilities from contracts and other dealings; this covers all duties.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r15.anchor: وتدل على وجوب الوفاء بالعهود والأمانات، فيدخل فيها جميع الأمانات والمضمونات من العقود وغيرها

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.claim: No other required duties are omitted: worship, contracts, and liabilities fall under trusts and covenants; sins fall under avoiding laghw.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.anchor: قلنا: لا؛ لأن جميع ما كلف دخل في الآية؛ لأن جميع ما يجب فعله من العبادات

MUQATIL:23:7-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:7-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:7-11/r2.claim: They preserve the performance of trusts and fulfill their covenants.
MUQATIL:23:7-11/r2.anchor: يقول: يحافظون على أداء الأمانة، ووفاء العهد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r1.claim: Meccan and Sahl read the word in the singular, “their trust”; others read the plural, “their trusts.”

NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r2.claim: The entrusted object and the matter pledged are themselves called a trust and a covenant; God’s command to return trusts to their owners illustrates the usage.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r2.anchor: سمى الشئ المؤتمن عليه والمعاهد عليه أمانة وعهدا ومنه قوله تعالى ان الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r3.claim: The wording covers every trust and covenant undertaken toward God or toward other people.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r3.anchor: والمراد به العموم فى كل ما ائتمنوا عليه وعوهدوا من جهة الله عز وجل ومن جهة الخلق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r4.claim: The guardians preserve what is entrusted; a shepherd safeguards and tends what is in his care.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p117#2/r4.anchor: حافظون والراعى القائم على الشئ بحفظ وإصلاح كراعى الغنم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:7-9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:7-9/r10.speaker: ابن كثير
QURTUBI-FULL:23:7-9/r10.claim: Most readers have the plural amānāt, while Ibn Kathir reads the singular amānah.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:7-9/r10.anchor: قرأ الجمهور «لأماناتهم» بالجمع. وابن كثير بالإفراد

QURTUBI-FULL:23:7-9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:7-9/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:7-9/r11.claim: Trusts and covenants include everything a person undertakes in religious and worldly matters, by word, deed, or belief; they cover dealings and promises, require faithful preservation and fulfillment, and trust is broader than covenant.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:7-9/r11.anchor: والأمانة والعهد يجمع كل ما يحمله الإنسان من أمر دينه ودنياه

QASHANI:23:1-11/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:1-11/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:1-11/r6.claim: The trusts are secrets God deposited in their innermost selves; the covenant is God's pledge at the beginning of primordial nature, to be fulfilled and brought to life.
QASHANI:23:1-11/r6.anchor: من أسراره التي أودعهم الله إياها في سرهم { وعهدهم } الذي عاهدهم الله عليه في بدء الفطرة

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r2.speaker: نافع وابن كثير
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read the trust term in the singular.

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r3.claim: The entrusted object and the commitment one has undertaken are themselves called a trust and a covenant.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r3.anchor: واعلم أنه يسمى الشيء المؤتمن عليه والمعاهد عليه أمانة وعهدا

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r4.claim: The Qurʾānic commands to return trusts and not betray them illustrate the term's usage.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r4.anchor: لا تخونوا الله والرسول وتخونوا أماناتكم

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r5.claim: A rāʿī is one who tends, preserves, and improves what is entrusted to him.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r5.anchor: والراعي القائم على الشيء لحفظ وإصلاح كراعي الغنم وراعي الرعية

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r6.claim: Trust covers everything whose neglect counts as betrayal, including all worship, whether hidden itself or hidden in the manner of its performance.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r6.anchor: واعلم أن الأمانة تتناول كل ما تركه يكون داخلا في الخيانة

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r7.claim: Examples of worship entrusted to a person include fasting, ritual bathing after sexual impurity, and completing ablution properly.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r7.anchor: لأنها إما أن تخفي أصلا كالصوم وغسل الجنابة وإسباغ الوضوء

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r8.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r8.claim: A Prophetic saying calls the person who does not complete his prayer the greatest betrayer.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r8.anchor: أعظم الناس خيانة من لم يتم صلاته

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says trust is the first thing lost from religion and prayer the last.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r9.anchor: أول ما تفقدون من دينكم الأمانة وآخر ما تفقدون الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r10.claim: Deposits, contracts, and other commitments made by deed or speech must be fulfilled.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r10.anchor: ومن جملة ذلك ما يلتزمه بفعل أو قول فيلزمه الوفاء به كالودائع والعقود

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r11.claim: A person is also entrusted to honor the words by which slaves are emancipated and women are made unlawful to him.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r11.anchor: ومن ذلك الأقوال التي يحرم بها العبيد والنساء لأنه مؤتمن في ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r12.claim: Covenant includes contracts, oaths, and vows.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r12.anchor: وأما العهد فإنه دخل فيه العقود والإيمان والنذور

RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r13.claim: Keeping these trusts and covenants counts toward attaining success.
RAZI-FULL:v23p71/r13.anchor: فبين سبحانه أن مراعاة هذه الأمور والقيام بها معتبر في حصول الفلاح

RAZI-FULL:v23p72/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p72/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p72/r6.claim: The seven listed qualities need not enumerate fasting, pilgrimage, and purity because trust and covenant encompass all duties and prohibitions, while purity falls under preserving prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v23p72/r6.anchor: يأتي على جميع الواجبات من الأفعال والتروك كما قدمنا

STUDYQURAN:23:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:8/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:8/r1.claim: A nearly identical verse appears at 70:32.
STUDYQURAN:23:8/r1.anchor: See the nearly identical verse in 70:32.

STUDYQURAN:23:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:8/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:8/r2.claim: The commentary points to 2:283, 4:58, and 8:27 on trusts.

STUDYQURAN:23:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:8/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:8/r3.claim: Covenant (ʿahd), pact (mīthāq), and promise or tryst (mīʿād) are important Quranic terms for the human relationship with God.
STUDYQURAN:23:8/r3.anchor: are significant aspects of the Quran’s language relating to the relationship between human beings and God

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r15.claim: Trusts differ: some concern outward duties, some inward subtleties, and others spiritual dealings, encounters, or communion.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r15.anchor: الأمانات مختلفة ، وعند كل أحد أمانة أخرى ، فقوم عندهم الوظائف بظواهرهم ، وآخرون عندهم اللطائف في سرائرهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r16.claim: Covenants differ: some pledge to worship only God, while others pledge to witness none but Him in either world.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r16.anchor: فمنهم من عاهده ألا يعبد سواه ، ومنهم من عاهده ألا يشهد في الكونين سواه

SULAMI:v2p31#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p31#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن الفضيل
SULAMI:v2p31#2/r1.claim: The organs are trusts: eyes avoid forbidden sights and reflect; ears avoid idle or obscene speech and attend remembrance; the tongue avoids slander and remembers; feet pursue obedience; the mouth consumes lawful things; hands avoid forbidden use and uphold right; the heart attends to God alone.
SULAMI:v2p31#2/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن الفضيل : جوارحك كلها أمانات عندك أمرك في كل واحد منها بأمر

SULAMI:v2p31#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p31#2/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p31#2/r2.claim: The covenant is to bear and preserve these trusts; whoever neglects a trust is characterized as unjust and ignorant.
SULAMI:v2p31#2/r2.anchor: ثم العهد عليك في حمل الأمانة وحفظها فمن ضيع الأمانة وصف بالظلم والجهالة

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.claim: The traits in the opening passage show faith as living and active, producing its effects so that the believer reaches the intended end, success.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية إلى تمام ثماني آيات تذكر من أوصاف المؤمنين ما يلازم كون وصف الإيمان حيا فعالا

TABATABAI:23:8-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r1.claim: Amanah originally is a verbal noun and here likely means entrusted property and similar trusts; its plural suggests the various kinds circulating among people.
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r1.anchor: وربما أريد به ما ائتمن عليه من مال ونحوه، وهو المراد في الآية، ولعل جمعه للدلالة على أقسام الأمانات

TABATABAI:23:8-11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r2.claim: A broader interpretation includes every divine duty and the entrusted use of one's body, faculties, and other people's property; the author finds it semantically sound but unlikely from the wording.
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r2.anchor: وربما قيل بعموم الأمانات لكل تكليف إلهي أؤتمن عليه الإنسان وما اؤتمن عليه من أعضائه وجوارحه

TABATABAI:23:8-11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r3.claim: In legal usage, a covenant is an obligation undertaken through a covenant formula, analogous to a vow or oath.
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r3.anchor: والعهد بحسب عرف الشرع ما التزم به بصيغة العهد شقيق النذر واليمين

TABATABAI:23:8-11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r4.claim: Covenant may instead mean all obligations binding a believer: God calls faith a covenant, and the singular suits the one covenant made through faith encompassing all duties.
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r4.anchor: ويمكن أن يراد به مطلق التكليف المتوجه إلى المؤمن فإن الله سبحانه سمى إيمان المؤمن به عهدا وميثاقا

TABATABAI:23:8-11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r5.claim: Ri'ayah means preservation; one etymology derives it from tending animals through feeding or warding off danger, but the author considers the reverse derivation more plausible.
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r5.anchor: وقد قيل إن أصل الرعي حفظ الحيوان إما بغذائه الحافظ لحياته أو بذب العدو عنه ثم استعمل في الحفظ مطلقا. انتهى. ولعل العكس أقرب إلى الاعتبار

TABATABAI:23:8-11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r6.claim: Believers preserve trusts from betrayal and covenants from breach; faith gives stability, so accepting a trust or pledge leaves one settled rather than wavering into treachery.
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r6.anchor: الآية تصف المؤمنين بحفظ الأمانات من أن تخان والعهد من أن ينقض، ومن حق الإيمان أن يدعو إلى ذلك

TABATABAI:23:1-11#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11#6/r6.claim: Social customs and laws answer recognized human needs; basic needs close to nature demand priority, and neglecting them causes greater harm than neglecting luxuries.
TABATABAI:23:1-11#6/r6.anchor: الذي يدعو الإنسان ويبعثه نحو الاستنان بالسنن الاجتماعية أو وضع القوانين الجارية في المجتمع البشري

TABRISI:23:1-3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
TABRISI:23:1-3/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the word in the singular here and in al-Maʿarij; others use plural.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير لأمانتهم على الواحد هنا وفي المعارج والباقون لأماناتهم على الجمع

TABRISI:23:1-3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:23:1-3/r3.claim: Abu Ali explains singular amana as a verbal and collective noun that covers many trusts; the plural is supported by 4:58.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: وجه الإفراد في الأمانة أنه مصدر واسم جنس فيقع على الكثرة

TABRISI:23:1-3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r4.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:23:1-3/r4.claim: The Prophet says entrusting a woman with her womb is a form of trust, illustrating singular usage for many instances and interpreting 2:228.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r4.anchor: ما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال من الأمانة أن أؤتمنت المرأة على فرجها

TABRISI:23:4-10/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:4-10/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:4-10/r9.claim: Believers preserve and fulfill trusts and covenants, including duties owed to God and to other people.
TABRISI:23:4-10/r9.anchor: أي حافظون وافون والأمانات ضربان أمانات الله تعالى وأمانات العباد

TABRISI:23:4-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:4-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:4-10/r10.claim: God’s trusts include fasting, prayer, and ritual washing; people’s include deposits, loans, sales, and testimony.
TABRISI:23:4-10/r10.anchor: فالأمانات التي بين الله تعالى وبين عباده هي العبادات كالصيام والصلاة والاغتسال

TABRISI:23:4-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:4-10/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:4-10/r11.claim: Covenants comprise God’s commands, personal vows, and agreements among people; all trusts and covenants must be fulfilled.
TABRISI:23:4-10/r11.anchor: وأما العهد فعلى ثلاثة أضرب أوامر الله تعالى ونذور الإنسان والعقود الجارية بين الناس

THALABI:v7p39/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p39/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p39/r10.claim: They faithfully preserve trusts placed with them and commitments and contracts they made with people.
THALABI:v7p39/r10.anchor: والذين هم لأماناتهم التي ائتمنوا عليها وعهدهم وعقودهم التي عاقدوا الناس عليها راعون حافظون وافون.

THALABI:v7p39/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p39/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
THALABI:v7p39/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir reads ‘trust’ in the singular, by analogy with the singular ‘their covenant.’
THALABI:v7p39/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير: لأمانتهم على الواحد لقوله: «وعهدهم» .

THALABI:v7p39/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p39/r12.speaker: الباقون
THALABI:v7p39/r12.claim: The other readers use the plural, supported by the Qur’anic command to return trusts to their owners.
THALABI:v7p39/r12.anchor: الباقون: بالجمع لقوله إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the trusts are deposits and other things entrusted to people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنها (¬2) أمانات الناس التي ائتمنوا عليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the trusts are obligations between God and a servant, hidden from others, such as ablution, ritual bathing, and fasting; most commentators prefer the people’s trusts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنها أمانات بين الله وبين عبده مما لا يطلع عليه إلا الله، كالوضوء والغسل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the word in the singular, أمانتهم; a singular verbal noun or collective can denote many trusts.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r4.claim: The singular collective can include God-to-servant duties such as fasting, prayer, and washing, and human rights such as deposits and goods held in trust; أمانة is a verbal noun used for its object.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r4.anchor: والأمانة تختلف ولها ضروب نحو: الأمانة التي بين الله وبين عبده كالصيام والصلاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r5.claim: The plural is supported by 4:58; the author also compares the singular collective at 6:108 with the plural أعمال at 23:63.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r5.anchor: ووجه الجمع قوله تعالى: {إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p528/r6.claim: أمانة is a verbal noun used to name the thing entrusted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says their عهد means the oaths taken from them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r1.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يقول وحلفهم الذي يؤخذ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes عهد as contracts they made with other people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r2.anchor: وقيل: يعني العقود التي عاقدوا الناس عليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says the root of ra‘y is taking responsibility to maintain and put right what is entrusted to one, whether a ruler’s subjects, a shepherd’s flock, or relations with another person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p529/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أصل الرعي (¬2) في اللغة: القيام على إصلاح

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p393#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p393#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p393#2/r1.claim: They discharge trusts and fulfill covenants.

ELMALILI:23:3-8/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r7.claim: Trusts are not limited to property; they include religious obligations, God's and people's rights, agencies, guardianships, and public offices.
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r7.anchor: “Emanet” yalnız mala münhasır değildir. Bütün tekâlîf-i şer‘iye, hukūkullah ve hukūk-ı ibâd, vekâletler, velâyetler, me’mûriyetler dahi emanetler cümlesindendir.

ELMALILI:23:3-8/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r8.claim: Covenants include contracts and commitments made to God, the Prophet, and other people.
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r8.anchor: gerek Allah’a ve Peygamber’e ve gerek nâsa karşı olan mukāvelât ve taahhüdâta şâmildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:8/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:8/r1.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:8/r1.claim: Exegetes take trusts and covenants to include entrusted material or spiritual things, agreements, and duties, as well as divine rulings to which believers commit themselves by professing faith; prayer and fasting are trusts too.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:8/r1.anchor: Müfessirler, buradaki emanet ve ahid kavramlarının hem insanlar tarafından korunması ve esirgenmesi için bırakılan nesneler

NAHHAS:v3p109/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p109/r10.speaker: المكيون
NAHHAS:v3p109/r10.claim: The Meccans read the singular لأمانتهم; the author says the verbal noun أمانة can serve for singular or plural, but plural is preferable because God entrusted people with many duties, including purification, prayer, and fasting.
NAHHAS:v3p109/r10.anchor: وقرأ المكيون ( لأمانتهم ) على واحدة قال أبو جعفر أمانة مصدر يؤدي عن الواحد والجمع فإذا أردت اختلاف الأنواع جاز الجمع والتوحيد إلا أن الجمع ههنا حسن

NAHHAS:v3p109/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p109/r11.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v3p109/r11.claim: Abū ʿUbayd supports the plural from 4:58, but al-Naḥḥās rejects the analogy: there it means specific deposited trusts; the singular عهدهم here also shows singular and plural are both possible.
NAHHAS:v3p109/r11.anchor: فأما احتجاج أبي عبيد في اختياره لأماناتهم بقوله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r1.claim: Their trusts include what has been entrusted to them in religious and worldly matters.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r1.anchor: ما ائتمنوا عليه من أمر الدين والدنيا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r2.claim: They honor their covenants and oaths and fulfill them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:8-14/r2.anchor: وحلفهم الذي يوجد عليهم راعون، يرعون ذلك ويقومون بإتمامه

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.claim: Umar describes revelation’s bee-like sound and the Prophet’s supplication, then reports that whoever upholds the first ten verses of al-Muʾminun enters Paradise.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.anchor: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - يقول

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r1.speaker: الكلبي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says trusts include obligations of belief, speech, conduct, property, family, dependents, relatives, neighbors, and other Muslims.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r1.anchor: ما روى الكلبي: كلُّ أحدٍ مؤتمن على ما افتُرض عليه من العقائد والأقوال والأحوال والأفعال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r2.speaker: السدي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r2.claim: Al-Suddi identifies all rights of the religious law as trusts that believers accept and undertake to fulfill through faith.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: إن حقوق الشرع كلها أمانات قد قَبِلَها المؤمن وضمن أداءها بقبول الإيمان.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r3.claim: Another view treats the body and other gifts God gives a person as trusts, betrayed when used outside their intended and permitted purpose.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r3.anchor: وقيل: كل ما أعطاه الله تعالى للعبد من الأعضاء وغيرها أمانة عنده، فمن استعمل ذلك في غير ما أعطاه لأجله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r4.claim: Trusts are plural because they are numerous and varied, while the covenant is singular; trusts precede it because of their importance and breadth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r4.anchor: فقد رأيت من تَعَدُّدها وتَنوُّعِها وتشعبها، ما يدعو إلى جمعها وليس كذلك العهد، فأفرد العهد وجمع الأمانة.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r5.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying faith is a trust and that a person without trust has no religion or faith.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r5.anchor: وحسبك من ذلك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الإيمان أمانة، ولا دين لمن لا أمانة له". وقوله: "لا إيمان لمن لا أمانة له"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r6.speaker: فتح القدير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r6.claim: Al-Fath al-Qadir states that trust is broader than covenant and every covenant is a trust.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r6.anchor: وجاء في (فتح القدير) : "والأمانةُ أعم من العهد، فكلُّ عهدٍ أمانة"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r7.claim: رَاعُونَ is chosen over حفظ because رعى originally means tending livestock and includes keeping, managing, and checking on what is entrusted.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r7.anchor: أما اختيار كلمة (راعون) مع الأمانة والعهد دون (الحفظ) الذي استُخدم مع الفروج، فله سبب لطيف ذلك أن (راعون) اسم فاعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r8.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf defines a guardian as one who cares for and improves what is entrusted, such as a shepherd or governor.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p148/r8.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) : "والراعي القائم على الشيء بحفظ وإصلاح، كراعي الغنم وراعي الرعية. ويقال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r1.claim: Trusts range from deposits and money to secrets, confidential speech, dependents, crops, public office, courts, and religious law; the author cites 33:72 on the trust.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r1.anchor: فمن ذلك ما يُؤْتَمَنُ عليه الشخص من ودائع الناس وأموالهم، ومنها ما يطّلع عليه من أسرار الناس وأحوالهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r2.claim: Guarding chastity and guarding trusts are linked: both should be protected, and failure in either makes a person blameworthy and transgressive.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r2.anchor: وجهُ ارتباط هذه الآية بما قبلَها ظاهر، إذ أن كلاًّ من الفروج والأمانات ينبغي أن يُحفَظَ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r3.speaker: البحر المحيط
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r3.claim: Al-Bahr al-Muhit says trust covers every entrusted matter, command, affair, religious or worldly, and the whole religious law.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p146/r3.anchor: جاء في (البحر المحيط) : "والأمانة الظاهر أنها كل ما يُؤْتَمَنُ عليه من أمر ونهي، وشأن ودين ودنيا، والشرع كله أمانة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r1.claim: Putting trusts and covenants before their guardian emphasizes their importance and that they are especially worthy of care.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r1.anchor: وأما تقديم الأمانة والعهد على (راعون) فللاهتمام والعناية بأمرهما، وللدلالة على أنهما أَولى ما يُرْعى في هذه الحياة.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r2.claim: The added lām emphasizes exclusive association and lets راعون mean that they are the owners and stewards of the trusts and covenants.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r2.anchor: وزيادة اللام، تفيد الزيادة في الاختصاص وتوكيده. وتفيد فائدة أخرى إلى جانب ما ذكرت

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r3.claim: Since راعي can mean an owner or person managing something, the phrasing means they are responsible holders of trusts and covenants; يرعون would not convey that nuance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r3.anchor: فيكون المعنى على هذا: والذين هم أصحاب الأمانات والعهود، أي: هم أهلها ومتولّوها.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r8.claim: The faithful keep every trust and promise, whether owed to God or to other people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r8.anchor: These people abide by all trusts and promises, whether they relate to God or to His creatures.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.claim: The next sūrah, al-Nūr, supplements this one: faith illuminating the inner self brightens individual and collective life, while its absence darkens both.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.anchor: Details of all these points will be found in the next sūrah: Sūrah al-Nūr which is the supplement of this sūrah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.claim: Islahi summarizes the earlier passage as a progression from inward faith through prayer, zakāh, restraint, fidelity, and guarded prayer to lasting success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.anchor: on them depends the success of the believers.

NASHR:v2p328/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p328/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p328/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the word for trusts in the singular in both al-Muʾminun and al-Maʿarij; the other readers use the plural.
NASHR:v2p328/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير فيهما بغير ألف على التوحيد

NASHR:v2p328/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p328/r2.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p328/r2.claim: The remaining readers read the word for trusts in the plural in both places.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p184/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p184/r3.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p184/r3.claim: Al-Razi includes sexual integrity, duties to God such as prayer and fasting, inward qualities such as sincerity and truthfulness, and human trusts such as deposits and goods among the trusts to be kept.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p184/r3.anchor: أو في المعاني الباطنة كالإخلاص والصدق , أو بينهم وبين خلق

BIQAI-FULL:v5p184/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p184/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p184/r4.claim: A covenant is the greatest trust, so it is singled out after the general mention of trusts; keeping it means fulfilling, preserving, and repairing it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p184/r4.anchor: ولما كان العهد أعظم أمانة , تلاها به تنبيها على عظمة فقال : { وعهدهم راعون * } أي الحافظون بالقيام والرعاية والإصلاح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p147/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p147/r8.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p147/r8.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī reports that amānāt is plural because trusts are numerous and varied for each person, whereas ʿahd is singular because it is less numerous or because it is a verbal noun.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p147/r8.anchor: وكأنه لكثرة الأمانة، جُمعت ولم يُجمع العهدُ، قيل: إيذاناً بأنه ليس كالأمانة كثرة، وقيل: لأنه مصدر
